item.title: Even during the beta, World of Warcraft Forever was shaping up to be huge, with an unprecedented amount of testers. But, over the weekend Blizzard announced that World of Warcraft Forever had the biggest launch in WoW history.
item.description:
Even during the beta, World of Warcraft Forever was shaping up to be huge, with an unprecedented amount of testers. Over the weekend, Blizzard announced that World of Warcraft Forever had the biggest launch in WoW history.
The news came over X/Twitter, where the official World of Warcraft account posted that Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history, both in terms of peak concurrent players and the number of returning players. Keep in mind that this history includes Wrath of the Lich King and Warlords of Draenor, both of which had huge launches – though the latter didn't exactly maintain it.
WoW Forever didn't just break records by dragging old players in and convincing them to resub. Holly Longdale, Blizzard's executive producer and vice president for World of Warcraft, posted her own statistic, saying, "Another statistic is filling our hearts – we are seeing the most NEW players for a WoW launch in 15 years!" That means WoW Forever has brought more players in than any WoW expansion since Cataclysm first launched 16 years ago in 2010.
Congratulations everyone, you made HISTORY!WoW: Forever has achieved:🔹The biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players🔹The highest number of returning players in WoW historyThis is all because of you, the players. From all of us, THANK YOU! https://t.co/MQxQXmNDbA
Scrolling through Longdale's replies, it's clear that people are loving WoW Forever. There are a ton of fans talking about how they played all weekend, like Dungeons and Dragons senior game designer Joey Haeck, who posted a picture of himself on a Zeppelin leaving Orgrimmar, saying, "Congratulations to the whole Forever team! I'm having a blast on every packed zeppelin and every open vista."
While we here at IGN don't have a full review yet, our early review is positive, with reviewer Len Hafer talking about her beta experience, saying, "I ended my beta journey at level 13, gazing out across the dusty plains of Westfall, because I didn't want to spoil too much for myself before the big day. But from what I have seen so far? I think they might have done it. They made me believe I can go home again – and that home is somewhere I want to spend more time, with new surprises to discover. Let's see if they can keep it up for 47 more levels. Watch this space for updates in the weeks to come."
While it's obviously been a huge success, Blizzard had been cooking World of Warcraft Forever on the back burner for a while, only pulling the trigger on its full development after it saw how successful Season of Discovery was back in 2023. Even with the massive load of players logging in at launch, WoW Forever had an extremely smooth launch, thanks to running on a massive amount of hardware. There was even a race to max level, which took three whole days before someone hit the level cap of 60.

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever has been a massive hit, and I've seen hundreds of players in pretty much every part of the game. After Blizzard massively nerfed dungeon experience early on in the Forever beta, the company has finally given it a bit of a buff, but it might not be enough.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever has been a massive hit, and I've seen hundreds of players in pretty much every part of the game. After Blizzard massively nerfed dungeon experience early on in the Forever beta, the company has finally given it a bit of a buff, but it might not be enough.
World of Warcraft Forever community manager Kaivax posted on the WoW forums that dungeon experience would be getting a 50% buff Sunday morning, which did help make dungeons a better way to level your character. But, as the community pointed out, even with this massive 50% buff, the dungeon experience you get is still way less than you'd get in the original version of World of Warcraft classic.
Back when World of Warcraft Forever was first announced, Blizzard's Kris Zierhut did an interview with The Sun talking about how experience from killing monsters in dungeons was "brought way down" The reason he gave for that change was wanting players to focus on leveling out in the open world, saying, "You’d be better off going to Shen’dralas or Riverglades or Hyjal instead of grinding a dungeon. We want people in the outdoor world meeting each other."
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
On October 8, Blizzard let up a bit, increasing dungeon experience by about 20%. But, because dungeon experience was already around 80% lower than it was on Classic, this 20% buff didn't actually make leveling in dungeons much more viable. Still, Blizzard left it at that level throughout the rest of the beta. Then, over the weekend, as WoW Forever players finally started doing dungeons, it was clear that they just weren't providing enough experience. Enter Sunday's 50% dungeon experience buff.
I actually ran dungeons both on Saturday and Sunday – Ragefire Chasm on Saturday and Ruins of Lordaeron on Sunday – and I did notice a difference. But even though I could tell that my experience bar was filling a bit slower, with the amount of time the dungeons take, you should be able to get one or two full levels out of them. And I'm not alone there; on Reddit, one player even did the math to figure out how far away dungeon experience is from Classic, even with the new buff.
According to aritalo on Reddit, even with the buffs, dungeon enemies are still only rewarding about a third of the experience they do in Classic.
Dungeon experience, even now, is extremely divisive in the community. User InterestingCell5247 writes, "The main problems with dungeons having nerfed exp rates is that its harder to find groups since if you already did the quests you have no reason to go back. But there are also knock-on effects like fewer people feeling incentivized to roll tanks and healers, because those roles generally sacrifice open world leveling speed/efficiency for easier access to dungeons."
Meanwhile, user ACoolGuy-Promise just wishes Blizzard was more clear on the final numbers, saying, "They can’t say “X percent“ of classic values? Just obfuscating this sh*t for no reason. This is barely a buff."
On the forums, however, there are players who are upset that Blizzard caved to the demand for more dungeon experience. For instance, player Kassa posted, "I knew blizzard would cave," and then followed that up by posting, "and I knew even this buff wouldn’t be good enough for the complainers. Blizzard, you have solved nothing. Now they just know to beg louder."
Only time will tell whether or not Blizzard will further buff dungeon experience in WoW Forever, but in the meantime, there does seem to be a ton of players out in the open world. But as more of them filter into World of Warcraft Forever, it's decisions like this that'll decide the shape of the MMO in the years to come. Blizzard has been pretty adament about not changing things that'd alter the spirit of the game, like group tagging. But with this experience change, along with the 20% buff in October, Blizzard is clearly open to tweaking the rate at which players gain experience.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time players are getting their hopes up after dataminers uncovered hints of Master Quest DLC – and maybe even some Majora's Mask content – tucked in the files of Nintendo's new remake.
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time players are getting their hopes up after dataminers uncovered hints of Master Quest DLC – and maybe even some Majora's Mask content – tucked in the files of Nintendo's new remake.
It's not been one week since Nintendo reimagined one of the most critically acclaimed games of all time for Nintendo Switch 2, and while some players are tearing it apart to look for glitches, others are digging even deeper. One of the first things dataminers did was sift through Ocarina of Time's files, and surprisingly, there may be some clues as to what remake plans Nintendo has in the cards.
There's a good chance you're here to see why we're talking about Majora's Mask today. We'll start by saying that you will want to keep expectations in check until an official announcement is made, but that shouldn't make YouTuber Austin John Plays' findings any less compelling (via Kotaku).
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Amiibo - Screenshots
Yesterday, the content creator uploaded a video meant to explore the in-game functionality of amiibo for the remake, including unreleased figures, of which there are (officially) two: one for Link, and one for Zelda. Considering the toys-to-life collectibles won't launch until 2027, anyone looking to access the masks they unlock would need to dive into the game's files to use them. This is the path Austin John Plays took – but he found more than just two new masks.
"I was starting to think that this was an Adult Link amiibo that's going to be released in the future," he said, referencing data containing strange, unused NPC dialogue. "I'm starting to not think that. I have a feeling this is one of those videos that I put it out, and in three years, I'm going to go like, 'Look! See? Crazy Austin? Crazy Austin was right!"
The code he referenced in the video alludes to characters calling out Link for wearing a "rare" and "otherworldly." Others call it "strange," with NPC Dampé even saying, "What's with that mask? Lookin' at it makes me feel weird." We do not know what this secret mask looks like or if the text tied to it will ever amount to anything…but with so much data on the backend, you can see why many believe Nintendo has already completed some amount of Majora's Mask content for some reason.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos
Again, this is all far from hard evidence, and even if it did point to something related to Majora's Mask, it's hard to say exactly what it may be. Austin John Plays theorizes the data we see here could be tied to a yet-to-be-announced Skull Kid amiibo for a yet-to-be-announced Majora's Mask remake. The idea here is that, like their Nintendo 64 counterparts, Nintendo's work on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake may have allowed it to quickly develop another remake based on Majora's Mask.
There's also the chance that Nintendo could simply release a standalone Skull Kid amiibo. The data could also point to another unique mask entirely – or it could point to nothing at all. Meanwhile, Bluesky user and dataminer @mrcheeze.github.io found their own clues that point to something entirely different: the return of Master Quest.
Master Quest is a remixed, harder mode for the original N64 Ocarina of Time that launched with the GameCube re-release. It reappeared with the Nintendo 3DS remake and then was confusingly absent from the Switch 2 remake. MyCheeze's findings suggest Nintendo could have plans to add it during an update, but dataminer @OatmealDome reported that their findings suggest players will need to own additional DLC in order to access it.
While Nintendo could distribute the DLC for free, I don't see why they went to the effort to make it be unlocked by DLC instead of just including it in an update...(w/ thanks to MrCheeze for initial finding)🦋 https://t.co/aWXyQTJ5Uk https://t.co/uMFAkhHdhX
Now, don't get all upset yet; we don't know if this alleged Master Quest DLC will have any particular cost tied to it. It could be $5 or even $20, or it could be some sort of bundle expansion. Nintendo has been known to offer add-on content via certain Nintendo Online subscription tiers, with one of the better examples being Switch 2 upgrades for both The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.
Oatmeal Dome also added that, based on their findings, the incomplete data also contained references to Master Quest featuring a mirrored world and modified dungeons. Again, it's been only about four days since The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake came to Switch 2. We will only know more with time, so don't go expecting Nintendo to announce Master Quest DLC or a Majora's Mask remake any time soon.
While we wait, you can read our review of the game here, or check out our look at the Biggest Changes from the original 1998 game. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas, and Early Item Bag Expansions. If you're looking for more, don't miss our complete guides to All Pieces of Heart, All Gold Skulltulas, and All Empty Bottles.
Should the next Zelda return to the more traditional format?

item.title: DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down from their roles as co-CEOs, with Skydance tapping an ex-Marvel exec to take over their duties.
item.description:
DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down from their roles as co-CEOs, with Skydance tapping an ex-Marvel exec to take over their duties.
Skydance confirmed the news in a press release, revealing that Gunn and Safran's last day as studio heads will be on December 1. Former Marvel exec Jeremy Latcham will replace them. Gunn and Safran are still overseeing post-production on Man of Tomorrow, which is directed by the former. They will also remain producers on other DC projects that are already in full swing, such as The Batman Part 2.
“James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of," said David Ellison, Chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, Co-CEO, of Skydance in a joint statement.
DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show
"We’re grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand. Jeremy has been a longtime creative partner to both, and we have complete confidence that James and Peter will ensure a smooth, collaborative transition and continue this work with care. We look forward to working with Jeremy to build the next generation of DC storytelling and to doubling down on our commitment to fans.”
Gunn and Safran also issued their own joint statement, acknowledging they have a history with Latcham from Gunn's days at Marvel.
“Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision," said the duo. "In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with.
9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU
"We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow.”
Gunn also released a more personal statement on his socials, where he noted that he has a great time building this universe, but also called the experience "trying" due to the corporate nature of it all. He also stated he is writing at least one more DC movie, but he isn't sure what is in store for him in this universe following the completion of that script.

item.title: BioWare veteran Mark Darrah has revealed an internal pitch for Dragon Age 4 that was never shared with fans.
item.description:
BioWare veteran Mark Darrah has revealed an internal pitch for Dragon Age 4 that was never shared with fans.
This pitch was shared in the form of a book which Darrah says was distributed within BioWare and to higher ups at EA. The idea behind the book was to “remain relevant” with the publisher, and to try and secure early funding and new hires for the project.
“There's always a fear, and I think a legitimate fear, within a big publishing organization that you will get cancelled or in, the in case of EA, you will simply be allowed to be to remain on a starvation diet to the point where you cannot continue,” Darrah said in a new video published to his YouTube channel.
“This is where ultimately this book comes into being,” he continued. “This was made in mid-2016 to be something that I could give to the team, but also something I could give senior people within the EA organization to say, ‘Look, we're doing a Dragon Age. Don't forget that Dragon Age: Inquisition was a super great game that sold super well, so you want another one, right?’"
Every IGN BioWare Game Review
The book focusses on what was then referred to as Joplin, the original plan for a fourth Dragon Age game. This was later cancelled in favour of a live service Dragon Age 4, which in turn, was partially scrapped and retooled in the single-player Dragon Age: The Veilguard.
As for Joplin, this book gives us an idea as to what BioWare was cooking behind the scenes. For starters, we can see that there was a chapter on the game having a "reactive world." However, in The Veilguard, reactions to decisions made in previous games were almost entirely scrapped.
Darrah also shared that BioWare envisioned destructable environements, dynamic weather conditions, and social interactions that went beyond the standard BioWare conversations. There’s even a reference to the player taking part in heists, something we haven’t seen in the series before.
With that said, Darrah admitted that many of these features would have been scrapped even if development went well. In fact, BioWare was in the process of phasing out heists in 2017. But it does show us the vision BioWare was chasing, with a desire to make the series much more immersive than previous entries.
While Darrah failed to reveal the full content of the books, he did share the opening he wrote back in 2016:
“Dragon Age: Inquisition has transformed what the franchise is and how it is perceived by the public. As we move forward, we have a great opportunity to continue the breakout we have started.
“We stand upon the foundation laid by Dragon Age: Inquisition. A foundation that lets us see further. To see things that didn't work and fix them, to see things that did work and improve them.
“The Dragon Age team will create a more immersive interactive world with people in it who act and react like real people. We have a lot of work to do, but never has a Dragon Age game started in a stronger place. This document represents our current thinking on the next steps of the franchise.”
Needless to say, the developers did not get the development cycle they were hoping for. Instead, Joplin was scrapped, and Dragon Age stagnated to make way for Mass Effect: Andromeda and Anthem. The Dragon Age series was put on ice after The Veilguard failed to reach EA’s sales targets.
Now, BioWare has been shut down by EA. Many fans are fighting to save BioWare’s work, particularly the now-cancelled Mass Effect Universe, but we certainly shouldn’t expect any developments in the Dragon Age series anytime soon.

item.title: Nintendo has teased a new LEGO Yoshi set in a post on the Nintendo Today! app.
item.description:
Nintendo has teased a new LEGO Yoshi set.
A news update posted to the Nintendo Today! app on Monday, November 9 is labelled "New LEGO Super Mario Set Hatching Soon," with the subtitle "Adults Welcome." Clicking into the post reveals a full chunk of Yoshi’s face in plastic brick form.
The teaser confirms that the set is a new addition to the Super Mario theme, owing to the rideable dinosaur’s debut in Super Mario World. However, the 'adult' focus of the teaser suggests the Super Mario line is branching out into more complex sets built for display.
There’s no word on pricing or release date, but based on the copyright information, we expect LEGO Yoshi to release in early 2027.
Note: The Nintendo App prevents screenshots or screensharing, so the above image is sourced from My Nintendo News.

item.title: Sony is releasing a new model of the PlayStation Portal in Japan next month. The big difference is that it has internal storage, hinting that Sony might be expanding the handheld’s functions in the future.
item.description:
Sony is releasing a new model of the PlayStation Portal in Japan next month. The big difference is that it has internal storage, hinting that Sony might be expanding the handheld’s functions in the future.
“With an eye towards future functionality, the new model comes with the brand new addition of internal storage,” teased Sony Japan’s official blog post. “We will provide further details regarding these future features as they are finalized.”
First released back in 2023 and looking like the stretch limo version of a PlayStation controller with an HD screen in the middle, the PlayStation Portal was originally designed as a way to play your PS5 games on handheld. Although this remote play function frees up your TV, it requires you to stream your games from your PS5 over Wi-fi.
The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time
In the official Playstation blog post announcing the new model, Sony emphasized that the Portal now allows “even players who don’t have a PS5” to enjoy PS5 games. Last year, Sony began giving PS Plus Premium members the option to stream games from the cloud to their PS Portal instead. With this new model release, Sony has also changed the full Japanese name of the handheld from “Playstation Portal Remote Player,” to simply “PlayStation Portal Player.” This suggests that the company is moving away from the Portal’s image as an accessory that streams from a PS5 console via Remote Play, to a more fully-fledged handheld.
It’s also possible that any new functions added to the PS Portal could be a testing ground for the upcoming PS6, which has long been rumored to involve a handheld. Back in June, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hideaki Nishino commented that developing new console experiences will involve “leveraging technologies that can be used in various forms and locations” and continuing to move the PlayStation brand beyond its common association of being played on a TV in the living room. More recently in October, there were rumors that Sony might have secured exclusive access to AMD’s next generation graphics tech for a new handheld.
In the meantime, the new PS Portal releases in Japan on December 10 and is up for preorder from November 13 at the same price as the current PS Portal (39,980yen). However, those interested in getting their hands on this model should note that it’s Japanese language only and requires a Japanese PSN account. It will be interesting to see if this new model makes it to other countries and regions.
Image credit: Sony Interactive Entertainment.
Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

item.title: Last month, Cyberpunk 2077 got an ambitious multiplayer mod, NightCoop. This is great if you want to play with up to eight players, going through the main story with friends. However, if you want something even more chaotic, we now have another multiplayer project: Open//77. This essentially turns Cyberpunk 2077 into GTA Online, letting servers of often more than 100 players mess around in Night City, getting up to various roleplay shenanigans.
item.description:
Last month, Cyberpunk 2077 got an ambitious multiplayer mod, NightCoop. This is great if you want to play with up to eight players, going through the main story with friends. However, if you want something even more chaotic, we now have another multiplayer project: Open//77. This essentially turns Cyberpunk 2077 into GTA Online, letting servers of often more than 100 players mess around in Night City, getting up to various roleplay shenanigans.
Open//77 was just released in alpha, meaning that anyone can now download it and give it a try themselves. You need to own both Cyberpunk 2077 and the Phantom Liberty expansion for it to work, but as long as that’s covered, you’re able to experience this new take on Night City.
While NightCoop is great if you want a pretty vanilla game experience, albeit with multiple Vs running around, Open//77 is more like a big playground. You have different roles and different tasks to get up to than in the base game. As you can also see in the footage, you can play in third-person.
Night City opens on November 6.Light RP, the official Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer server. Make your crew, race, run contracts, hit the casino, rob Arasaka, fight a world boss, outrun the NCPD.Friday, 22:00 UTC https://t.co/WpR4rB1DJA
It also looks like there’s more of a focus on just hanging out in the open world. One video shows players meeting up in a room they rented to play a board game. There are also more aesthetic features to play around with, such as an expanded vehicle customisation menu.
level -1 of the card shop: private rooms. neon deck, cozy lounge, tatami room. open one, send the code to a friend to play together https://t.co/OVy8ECkHuj
Vehicle customization is landing on Open77 @CyberpunkGame multiplayer. Any server can use it. RP, racing, car meets, whatever you're building. Open alpha and our Light RP server go live tonight, 22:00 UTC. https://t.co/Qrf2PLnoFt
Every server has its own theme. The most popular is NCRP, which supports up to 1,000 players looking to roleplay. Others are more combat, PvP focussed. Something to consider if you are interested is that Open//77 openly admits to using AI in the development process. Indeed, AI is why we are seeing so many fan-made projects like this released at once. It has divided the modding community, as many were making unofficial multiplayer mods like this long before generative AI was a factor. Earlier this month, Nexus Mods, the biggest platform for mods on the internet, reacted by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.
I tried Open//77 out, but it did not play nice with my heavily modded setup. Open//77 does support mods (and you can even temporarily download a host’s mods if you join their server), but messing around with my own mods so soon after having to fix them for the latest official update seemed a bit too daunting just now.
Wherever you land on projects like this, it’s no wonder there is an appetite for them. Cyberpunk 2077 was supposed to get an official multiplayer mode, but this was scrapped after the base game’s messy launch. A sequel is in development now, so we’ll have to wait and see if CD Projekt Red can make it work for that.
Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

item.title: LEGO has approved a LEGO Ideas submission based on the Christopher Nolan movie Interstellar. It will become an official LEGO set at some point in the future.
item.description:
LEGO has announced the winners of the LEGO Ideas First 2026 Review Stage. These sets originated as fan designs through the LEGO Ideas program, and have now been approved for official release. Among the newly announced upcoming sets is one based on the Christopher Nolan movie Interstellar. The other two sets to get approval during this review stage were Tulip Field Windmill and Chinese Cork Carving Art. As yet, there’s no word on pricing or official release dates for the newly approved sets.
LEGO Ideas Sets Approved for Official Release
Interstellar by Minibrick41587
Tulip Field Windmill by HisBrickMaterials
Chinese Cork Carving Art by GenericBrix
The Interstellar set was submitted by fan designer Minibrick41587. It includes the wedge-shaped Ranger spacecraft from the movie, along with minifigures for the Matthew McConaughey character Cooper and the Anne Hathaway character Dr. Brand. Also included are the robot companions TARS and CASE.
LEGO Interstellar Set
While Interstellar wasn't immediately appreciated as one of Christopher Nolan's best films after its 2014 release (we gave it an 8/10 in our review), there's been a growing appreciation for the film in recent years among fans and critics. This LEGO set's approval may be another sign of its improving standing.
New Additions to the LEGO Ideas Parking Lot
The 5th Element: Korben Dallas Taxi by MarinBrickDesign
Peashooter by DistinguishedCrow
During this latest review stage, LEGO placed two additional LEGO Ideas submissions in the Parking Lot. These sets are The 5th Element, which features a flying taxi and a Multi Pass from the movie, and Peashooter, based on a weapon from the video game Plants vs. Zombies. The Parking Lot is where sets go when they “need a little longer to work through the review process.” They’ll stay in the Parking Lot until a final decision is made.
Other Sets Currently in the Parking Lot
Lunch Atop a Skyscraper
Hollow Knight: A Journey to Hallownest
Bob’s Burgers Grand Reopening
Naruto: Ichiraku Ramen Shop
Parking Lot sets may end up being approved or not. But a set being put in the Parking Lot doesn’t say anything about its quality. The recently approved LEGO Daft Punk set had previously been in the Parking Lot.
We’ve just about reached the end of the line for new 2026 LEGO releases. The only remaining set scheduled to come out this year is the 2026 Black Friday LEGO set, LEGO Godzilla. However, a number of sets have been announced for January 2027 and beyond; see our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far for more info.
Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games, LEGO sets, and 4K Blu-rays. You can follow him on Bluesky.

item.title: GTA 6 preloads are live for those who live in New Zealand (or are pretending to live in New Zealand to play early) and fans are scanning the game files for new information.
item.description:
GTA 6 preloads are live for those who live in New Zealand (or are pretending to live in New Zealand to play early) and fans are scanning the game files for new information. Of course, the files are encrypted so they can only tell us so much.
The main takeaway is how much space each of the things in GTA 6 takes up. Rockstar has announced that GTA 6 weighs in at up to 212 GB, “depending on your device.” But following the release of the preload today, it was reported that the audio file alone is 22GB.
Elsewhere, one Rockstar fan believes that because the files for story content are separated out from the main game files, the same will be true for the inevitable next version of GTA Online. This would suggest that you’ll eventually be able to install single-player and Online separately.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
An account focused on reporting PlayStation game file sizes also noticed “intentType": "launchMultiplayerActivity," seemingly confirming Online’s eventual appearance in GTA 6. Rockstar has been completely silent on the existence of GTA Online for GTA 6, but the enduring success of GTA 5’s online portion means it’s safe to assume it’ll happen at some point.
Interestingly, a file named "core_restofworld001" is missing from the Australia & New Zealand version of GTA 6, perhaps suggesting there's cut content in those regions. Another fan noticed that BVH8 will be supported in GTA 6. BVH8 specifically makes ray tracing work better on PS5 Pro, which Ubisoft used for Assassin’s Creed Shadow’s PS5 Pro support.
“By itself, the PS5 Pro's faster GPU helps performance without much effort from developers, but the game changing technology is the improved ray tracing capabilities of the PS5 Pro that BVH82 offers over BVH4,” Ubisoft said at the time. “With our implementation of BVH8 support on PS5 Pro, we were able to speed up GPU tasks involving hardware ray tracing usage by about 300%.”
Officially, all we know about PS5 Pro support is the confirmation from Sony that GTA 6 will feature “PS5 Pro Enhanced Support.” Unfortunately, there’s been no word on what exactly that means. Indeed, Rockstar has yet to announce resolution and frame rate details for GTA 6 on any platform.
However, those hoping for higher frame rates might be disappointed. According to experts, it’s unlikely GTA 6 will go higher than 30fps on any platform because of its ray tracing and physics simulations.
While you wait for GTA 6’s November 19 launch, there’s still a small chance you might be able to bag some GTA 6 merch from Selfridges, but it’s selling out fast. And we've got all the information you need on the GTA 6 preload global release times, as well as details on the physical poster.

item.title: The lead animator for Mass Effect 2 has shared a previously unreleased trailer for the game, only ever seen by the developers at BioWare.
item.description:
The lead animator for Mass Effect 2 has shared a previously unreleased trailer for the game, only ever seen by the developers at BioWare.
This trailer, described as a demo reel of the in-progress cinematics, dates back to April 2009. It would have been used to demonstrate the kind of work that the animation team was doing for Mass Effect 2, and eagle-eyed fans will notice several scenes that did make it into the final game.
Fuck it - here's something for #N7Day I haven't shown before. A very pre-alpha internal trailer intended to highlight the cinematics we were creating in Montreal.Faces were the average of all the customisation sliders in Maya, and we ran every scene with each possible squamate when polishing.
Released by Jonathan Cooper, a game developer who has worked with the likes of BioWare, Ubisoft, and Naughty Dog, this Mass Effect 2 trailer gives us an incredibly early look at some of the game’s characters and pivotal moments. While it can be a little hard to make out, we can spot companions like Miranda, Garrus, and Jack.
Cooper hasn’t shared too much info on the trailer, but did say what it was like to work on it. “[…] remembering all the arguments and drama on the team haha,” he said. “But mostly reading the scripts and getting pumped imagining how awesome we could make Shepard look hitting those story beats.”
Mass Effect 2 was quite the departure from the first game, and this internal trailer makes that perfectly clear. After opening with Shepard’s death, we’re treated to a very ‘00s action movie monologue from the Commander themself, before cutting to the new Normandy crew.
Every IGN BioWare Game Review
If you’re curious about the song in the background, it’s C'Mon Try A Little Bit by Melodrone. It doesn’t appear to have been used in any of the promotional material that was shared with fans back in the day, and it only has 64,000 plays on YouTube.
All in all, this is nothing like the trailer we would be shown, cinematic or otherwise, but it does capture that edgier, action vibe that the sequel was going for, compared to its more optimistic predecessor. It’s a vibe that continues to resonate with fans to this day, as Mass Effect 2 is often held up as the best game BioWare ever put out.
Now, those same fans are fighting to protect the series they love. After EA closed BioWare and canceled Mass Effect 5, the community started the Save Mass Effect campaign, which urges the publisher to do something with the series, whether that’s fund new games or licence it out to another developer. Some are also pushing for Mass Effect to be returned to those who worked on it.
Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

item.title: Luxury British department store Selfridges has had the ground floor of its flagship London store overtaken by GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 release date. It’s not just a little display, either; Rockstar and the retailer have gone all-out.
item.description:
Luxury British department store Selfridges has had the ground floor of its flagship London store overtaken by GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 release date. It’s not just a little display, either; Rockstar and the retailer have gone all-out.
The front of the installation at 400 Oxford Street has a blue Grotti Cheetah Classic parked in the window — the exact car seen driving around Miami to promote GTA 6. There’s VI signage and Vice City iconography all over the store.
Good morning from Selfridges London #GTA6 https://t.co/dbQcQGhIaj
Live from Selfridges at Oxford Street for the #GTAVI activation🌴Rockstar are not messing around 🤯 https://t.co/vqqXKwB1oJ
In total, there are over 60 GTA 6-themed items for sale, from clothing to luggage tags. The most expensive item is an exclusove Goodtime State Varsity Jacket that costs an eye-watering £2,500 (approx. $3,355).
The GTA 6 activation opened at the Selfridges Bond Street shop this morning, with the online Selfridges GTA 6 merch going live at the same time. There are basketballs, bags, mugs, and a wide range of clothing options.
Launch saw queues of over 100,000 people and some of the items have sold out as a result, but queue times have at least died down now. Many of the items on sale are exclusive to Selfridges, making them a must-buy for hardcore collectors. At the time of this article's publication, the £2,500 jacket is sold out.
GTA 6 Launch Screenshots
It’s the first major activation in the UK. Previously, Rockstar focused most of its efforts on Miami, the metropolis GTA 6’s Vice City is based on.
In September, Rockstar paid just shy of $1 million to install a massive, glowing "Welcome to Vice City" sign on top of the Miami Heat's arena, the Kaseya Center. The arena will also be home to an unprecedented NBA game sponsored by Rockstar Games.
On November 18, the Miami Heat will play a regular season game against the Milwaukee Bucks on a Vice City-themed court with never-before-seen jerseys inspired by GTA 6. The arena will also be selling Vice City merch, with Rockstar and the NBA labeling the event as a "night in Vice City."
We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park, how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme, and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely.
Image credit: Selfridges.

item.title: A popular Nintendo blogger who tells his viewers obscure facts about Super Mario has been hit with serious health conditions, including heart failure. The online personality has vowed to continue running the blog for as long as he’s able.
item.description:
A popular Nintendo blogger who tells his viewers obscure facts about Super Mario has been hit with serious health conditions, including heart failure. The online personality has vowed to continue running the blog for as long as he’s able.
Supper Mario Broth is a blog and series of social media accounts known for posting arcane and funny trivia about everyone’s favorite Italian plumber. The blog has shared thousands of facts from the series since its creation in 2012.
In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2, it is possible to play the ocarina using Dry Bones in Super Mario Maker 2. https://t.co/wv0RYNeSyM
“I am scared I will soon not be able to see Mario again,” he said in a post to his 270,000 X / Twitter followers. “However, I promise that until that day arrives, I will always be here, posting Mario facts. Thank you all so much for your support through the years.”
Despite a healthy lifestyle, the condition is genetic. According to the blogger, there’s a two-in-three chance he survives past one year.
The condition is also affecting his eyesight, degrading it over time. He isn’t sure whether surgery or medication can stop or slow this process yet.
“Since being able to see well is fundamental to my ability to both myself research Mario games and compile the discoveries of others, this may affect my ability to run Supper Mario Broth in the future,” he said. “However, I will never forget the promise I made to you: I will continue to run Supper Mario Broth for as long as I’m physically able to.”
The blogger continued to say that “sharing [Mario] findings is my only purpose,” but noted that the condition may cause gaps in the content.
Supper Mario Broth didn’t ask for any financial or emotional support in this difficult time. “I already have all the support I could need,” he said. “All I can do is hope for my frail body to overcome this.
“I hope with all my (failing) heart that I can continue doing this for years to come,” he said. “And if I should one day stop posting: thank you very much for reading.”
Thousands of supportive replies have poured in, thanking the blogger for his work and integrity. There’s fan art, messages of support, and even people pressuring Nintendo to let the blogger play whatever in-development Mario game it’s cooking up.
Photo by BEHROUZ MEHRI/AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: Father Arrested After Leaving Sleeping 6-Year-Old Daughter in Line for Pokémon Cards
item.description:
A South Carolina man has been arrested and accused of leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target store overnight to hold his place in line for Pokémon cards, it has been reported.
According to the Washington Post, John-Michael Dooley, 35, had been waiting with his daughter outside the store this past Friday in Charleston's West Ashley district, where a throng of Pokémon fans had slowly gathered overnight in anticipation of a newly released set of the popular trading cards.
A news release from the Charleston Police Department states that officers arrived at the store around 2:30am after receiving reports of an unattended child. Witnesses at the scene told police that Dooley handed his daughter a blanket and a pillow sometime after 1am, before leaving her asleep in his spot in line. Wheen Dooley failed to return after an hour, these concerned witnesses were forced to contact the authorities.
Eventually Dooley returned to the store and was promptly arrested. In an interview with authorities, he admitted to police that he had gone home and left his young daughter unattended so that he could hold his spot in the line, according to the Charleston Police.
Dooley was then charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. Police said that the girl was unharmed and immediately placed into emergency protective custody.
Pokemon Happy Meal Cards 2026
This shocking act of Pokémon card-related parental neglect is in stark contrast to last week's news that the father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid had made a very moving plea to The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son. On his Instagram, Avery's father Christian Garcia said, "I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much." At the time of writing, there has been no official response from the Japanese company in regarding Garcia's request.
Pokémon Trading Cards, which is currently celebrating its 30th anniversary, was recently announced as one of this year's inductees into National Toy Hall of Fame, alongside Bingo, Care Bears, and the classic slide, and beating out nominees like Bop It!, mahjong, and Polly Pocket.
"Pokémon TCG’s widespread appeal and global presence are undeniable," said curator Mirek Stolee. "The Pokémon TCG successfully adapted card game formulas established by its predecessors, making it more accessible and infusing it with the lovable Pokémon creatures."
Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. item.title: U2 guitarist The Edge apparently had such a good idea for Elf 2 that he went out of his way to write his own script.
item.description:
U2 guitarist The Edge apparently had such a good idea for Elf 2 that he went out of his way to write his own script.
That's according to Elf actor and Dancing with the Stars legend Andy Richter, who spilled the beans about the musician's fondness for Christmas during an episode of The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast. It's a pairing no one ever saw coming but one that apparently still happened – or at least it almost happened.
Richter said the story of The Edge (real name: David Howell Evans) and his secret Elf 2 script comes from producer and frequent Will Ferrell collaborator Shauna Robertson. When exactly the elusive script would have been written is unclear.
"She was in Europe, and somebody reached out to her and said, 'The Edge from U2 has written a sequel to Elf, and he wants to talk to you about it.' It's the weirdest story, but apparently, it was fully written," Richter recalled. "Somewhere in the world, there is an Edge-penned Elf 2 out there, which I would love for that to make the light of day."
If you're unfamiliar with the guitarist or the group he's helped define for the last 50 years, U2 is the Irish rock band behind megahits like With Or Without You, I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For, Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where The Streets Have No Name, and more. He's a legendary guitar player behind a long list of instantly recognizable songs, and by comparison he's got little to no experience in the movie world.
A proper, fully written film script for Elf of all things marks a trip through mostly uncharted territory for The Edge. Unfortunately, it doesn't sound like his words will ever jump off the page and onto screens, and it's unclear if we'll ever get to read the supposed story for ourselves.
The Best Christmas Movies and TV Episodes of the 2000s
"It never happened," Richter continued. "It's just one of those things where she's like, 'All right, sure. I'll meet him,' you know? And then it just petered out and never, never happened."
Richter said he's on the side of Christmas fans who say "let it be." Directed by Jon Favreau and starring Ferrell, Elf is a holiday phenomenon which has yet to be matched in terms of sheer popularity, and that's probably why we may never see a sequel made. The Buddy the Elf star himself told IGN in 2016 that he never found the idea of following up the early 2000s classic with a full-on sequel.
"Now that that time has passed, I think that the movie has become so special that I think that people – and I think rightfully so – loathe to mess with it. Because we all can think of movies that have been tarnished by their sequels. This is so special and so perfect, and so beloved; why risk it?"

item.title: Denis Villeneuve Praises Human Creativity Over AI Prompts, Almost Announces New Bond
item.description:
Denis Villeneuve has praised human creativity over AI prompts, and playfully stirred the pot over the increasing rumours and speculation surrounding the casting of the main character in his upcoming James Bond film.
Addressing the crowd at Saturday night's Art+Film fundraiser at the LACMA museum in Los Angeles where he was being honored for his contributions to cinema (thanks, THR), the Dune: Part Three director took the opportunity to praise his heroes including Steven Spielberg and James Cameron, before speaking to the existential crisis currently being suffered by artists as a result of the rise of artificial intelligence.
"At the heart of every one of my films, there’s a question I need to answer," said Villeneuve. "The audience may see it or they may not, and that is fine. For me, each film is a statement to the unknown to try and find that answer. Perhaps those questions are more urgent now than ever."
"We are at the crossroad, asking what defines a human being and what human expression is worth? Every parent on Earth is a little worried about the world of our children will inherit. That question is at the heart of Dune: Part Three with Paul and Chani fighting to give their children a better world than the one they were given.”
The director went on to discuss the vital role that human creativity plays in the process of creating art.
“For a filmmaker today, it is very real," said Villeneuve. "I have a choice. I can create something with a prompt or I can go into the desert with actors, with a crew and go on a real adventure where I learn about life and become better at my craft. Those are two different things. Well, I know there’s producers in the room and they will say that one is more expensive than the other. More important than the result is the process. The process is how the human experience acquires its meaning. In this moment in time, it is more important than ever that human beings keep making art together. That is the heritage I want to give to my children.”
On a more lighthearted note, Villeneuve closed his speech by referencing the growing hype surrounding the casting of the next James Bond. Playing up to the headlines, Villeneuve said, "To express my gratitude with the blessing of my new friends at Amazon, I will reveal to you tonight who will be the next James Bond. The new James Bond is… and I will stop right now because Amy Pascal is about to have a heart attack. Thank you very much.”
Just last week it was reported that The Batman's Robert Pattinson had screen-tested for the role of 007 in the 26th James Bond film, and that Superman's Nicholas Hoult had also come into consideration. The two join Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O'Connor on the shortlist for the hotly-contested role, although nothing official has been confirmed by Amazon MGM Studios.
Casting for James Bond has been underway since spring, and since then rumours about who will take the role of the British super spy have been flying around from all angles like misfiring gadgets in Q Branch. Slow Horses' Jack Lowden would appear to be the frontrunner at least based on the feedback from fans, although former Bond Daniel Craig appears to be rooting for Josh O'Connor.
Meanwhile, Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three is set to arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026. Also arriving in theaters around that time are three Dune: Part Three popcorn buckets, including one with two sandworm mouths. Watch those teeth.

item.title: Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
item.description:
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
The tech giant's board confirmed the news in a statement today, saying that it is looking into its concerns "in light of recent reporting" that Huang has "been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The update follows a late-October New York Times report, which stated the CEO had been unfaithful to his wife with an individual that U.S. intelligence believed to be involved in a Chinese spy plot.
The individual named in the report as having a relationship with Huang was Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. The CEO confirmed the affair in a letter sent to Nvidia staff (via BBC).
"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children,” he said. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
"Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation," he added. "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."
Nvidia said that a committee of independent directors would oversee the effort with the assistance of outside independent counsel. The board said that it currently has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."
The full statement follows: "The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
Nvidia RTX Spark
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.
"Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate."
Huang will remain Nvidia CEO as the investigation continues. The New York Times' report said that, as of last year, U.S. officials did not believe he was aware of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.
Photo by Joel Saget / AFP via Getty Images.

item.title: New videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan's Ricardo Tubbs driving a white Ferrari Testarossa, the wrong car for the period of the TV series that director Joseph Kosinski’s film is retelling. And there’s likely a legal reason for that.
item.description:
New videos from the set of Miami Vice ‘85 reveal Austin Butler’s Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan's Ricardo Tubbs driving a white Ferrari Testarossa, the wrong car for the period of the TV series that director Joseph Kosinski’s film is retelling. And there’s likely a legal reason for that.
In the first two seasons of the 1980s TV series, Don Johnson’s detective Sonny Crockett drove a black 1972 Ferrari Daytona Spyder convertible before it was blown up by a Stinger missile in the Season 3 premiere. (Cue the gaping Crockett meme.)
In the show’s canon, Crockett’s cars were seized assets from criminals and loaned to him by the Miami-Dade Police Department as part of his undercover identity. The department supplied Crockett with a white 1986 Ferrari Testarossa in the second episode of Season 3.
🚨| Austin Butler and Michael B. Jordan back on the streets of Brooklyn filming ‘Miami Vice ‘85’ 🎬🌴Sonny Crockett and Ricardo Tubbs, the city is yours 😎🔥 https://t.co/AWnbL6W400
The Daytona Spyder seen on the show, however, was a replica built on a Corvette C3 chassis since Ferrari North America refused to provide the show with an authentic model. Ferrari launched a legal battle against the show and the replica builder, McBurnie Coachcraft, citing trademark infringement and brand dilution.
“They eventually settled the dispute, winning broad legal protections for their trademarks and even the ‘shape and profile’ of the car,” recapped by @CinemaIsLife on X. “As a part of the settlement they donated two authentic Testarossas (their new flagship car) to the production—but only on the condition that the fake Daytona be dramatically blown up on national television.”
It would appear then that Universal is simply avoiding another legal headache by jettisoning the Daytona Spyder from Miami Vice ‘85 and going with the white Testarossa even though it violates canon.
Miami Vice ‘85 has been filming in New York and New Jersey but will shift production to Miami once hurricane season is over. The film opens in theaters, including IMAX, on May 19, 2028.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad."
item.description:
Jesse Eisenberg said he will "sometimes experiment with AI" – but it's just because he's "testing it to make sure it's bad."
The Batman v. Superman and A Real Pain star explained why he finds the rapidly advancing and controversial technology unnerving – and how he deals with it – during a conversation with Variety. As he continues to plant his feet in Hollywood as a talent who can act, write, and direct, AI is something he's trying to keep his eye on in more ways than one.
"I have a paranoid answer for this," Eisenberg said when asked if he's nervous about the technology. "I’m totally paranoid. I sometimes experiment with AI to see whether it's good at writing. And it's still not.
"I’m paranoid, so I check and it still isn't. Thank God. I say, 'Write a scene like this.' I'm just testing it to make sure it's bad, and it's still bad. So I'm relieved, but, like, how far away is it from being good? How far are we from a kid putting on a pair of goggles and saying, 'I want to watch a movie about me where I rob a bank and then kiss the girl I’m in love with at school. Here are pictures of her, here are pictures of me' and then they press play? I'm paranoid about that."
While figures like George Lucas have supported AI in the past, there are plenty of entertainers who have spoken out against the technology as it has advanced in recent years. Goku's voice actor in Dragon Ball, Masako Nozawa, blasted those who had used AI to steal her voice for their own use. Nicolas Cage said he'll "probably not work with" Amazon again after he declined to sign its AI waiver. Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto said Nintendo would prefer to "go in a different direction" when speaking about the topic in September.
Eisenberg elaborated on his approach, saying that there are two saving graces: the power of the creative spirit and art that has stood the test of time. As AI development progresses to new and often intimidating places, these are the things that bring him some peace.
The Biggest Movies Coming in 2026
"Creative spirit will find ways to entertain and delight us and speak about things in a way that maybe computers won’t," he added. "The other thing I think about all the time, and [The Debut star Julianne Moore is] about to go to a play in New York, is that I do these Greek plays, which were written 2,500 years ago and we perform them the same way they were performed 2,500 years ago. If they’ve lasted that long, they’ll still be there.
"People want to be in the same room as other people, watching and listening to stories. It’s as old as cave people sitting by the campfire telling stories, and there will always be room for that. What I do worry about is whether we’ll still be able to make a living from it. I’m not 100% sure about that."
Eisenberg's next movie is The Debut, which is set to arrive December 11, 2026. In related news, the moviemaker recently reflected on how winning a Razzie for his role as Lex Luthor affected his career. In June, he talked about what it was like to turn down an opportunity to return as Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network sequel.

item.title: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he thinks innovation at Sony shouldn't come "from making a PS6 for $1,200" but from making "another PS5 for $300."
item.description:
Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he thinks innovation at Sony shouldn't come "from making a PS6 for $1,200" but from making "another PS5 for $300."
As tech costs skyrocket and rumors of pricey gaming consoles swirl, the former president and CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment America took the time on The Trophy Room podcast to encourage the PlayStation maker to consider an unexpected, cheaper course of action. Pointing out how previous hardware leaps have typically offered clearly identifiable innovative qualities from generation to generation, he touched on why the PlayStation 6 simply leaning on "more ray tracing and more teraflops" might not be the best idea.
As Layden put it, "I think we have enough power in the machine."
PlayStation 5 Japan-Exclusive Midnight Black – Photos
"The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200. It's to make another PS5 for $300," he added. "Now, that would be true innovation. This is the first platform that I've seen that has gone up in price over time. I mean, PS2, at the end of the PS2 era, it was $99. You could buy a PS2 for $99."
The PS5 launched almost exactly six years ago with two primary options for players to choose from: a base version with a disc drive for $499, and a Digital Edition for $399. What seemed like relatively fair price points in 2020 now seems almost like a steal thanks to a series of price increases in recent years. Today, buying a base PS5 directly from PlayStation costs $649, a Digital Edition costs $599, and a Pro costs an unbelievable $899 (up $200 from its reveal price). Things get even worse when you look at retailers like GameStop.
Sony has put the blame on "continued pressures in the global economic landscape," but that's done little to lessen the sting for the average buyer. As console sales for Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo suffer, Layden is of the mind that Sony shouldn't be looking for a way to get to a likely more expensive future but instead a cheaper past.
LEGO PlayStation vs. the Original Console
"I think if I were in their shoes, that's what I'd be doing. I'd be trying to find a way to get the cost down on the 5," he added.
Later, he continued: "It's a hard place to be right now, I think. What the company needs to do is do what it's never done, which is, don't iterate the console. Make it smaller, make it cheaper, do all the things you can around that, but the silicon's fine, the OS is fine. It's more than enough power to build the kind of games all of us want to play."
If you look at the raw console release timeline, we're just about due for the next PlayStation, but many players say they don't want to see a PS6 announced until hardware prices come down. In May, Sony said it was still trying to decide when its next console should launch. It followed a February report that stated the company was considering pushing the device to 2028 – or even 2029 – following previous 2027 launch expectations.
